reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it documents and evaluates a Polkadot advertising campaign conducted with Brave Browser, including its formats, audience reach, and reported results. Its discussion of crypto, tokens, participation interest, and website engagement is presented as campaign subject matter and performance measurement, not as a request for money, credentials, or entry into an investment scheme.

citations.quote: Today we are happy to have with us the team from Brave Browser. And they're here to discuss a recent campaign that they ran for the Polkadot ecosystem on Brave.
there's data as a result of the spend
the new type takeover has the highest visibility because it goes out to our entire audience globally
the notifications achieved a CTR of 3.24% which is very strong

opening.argument: The presentation links crypto-related value claims to a concrete path for viewer participation. Brave is described as a system intended to “give that value back to our users,” while the accompanying description directs viewers to “Get Started on Polkadot” and to “Explore the Polkadot platform.” Read together, this is more than neutral reporting: it frames engagement with the Polkadot ecosystem as the route to obtaining or accessing value. The campaign’s own objective was to drive users to participate in Polkadot projects, making the external resources a solicitation pathway rather than merely background information.

citations.quote: Brave thought of a system utilizing the basic attention token where we can give that value back to our users.
three to four brave users are at least somewhat likely to participate in Polkadot projects
Get Started on Polkadot: https://polkadot.com/get-started
Explore the Polkadot platform: https://polkadot.com/platform

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a campaign does not remove the solicitation. The presenters explicitly discuss users’ likelihood of participating in projects, and the description supplies “Get Started” and platform links. Reporting clicks and visits describes how effectively the funnel worked; it does not establish that the promoted crypto participation was safe or that the promised value was actually delivered.

citations.quote: three to four brave users are at least somewhat likely to participate in Polkadot projects
Get Started on Polkadot: https://polkadot.com/get-started
the notifications achieved a CTR of 3.24% which is very strong

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The value statement concerns Brave’s advertising model, not a promise that viewers will earn by buying Polkadot assets. The campaign report measures awareness, clicks, and visits, while the description merely lists informational resources. Nothing cited requires a deposit, token purchase, or financial return, so the pathway described does not establish a scam category.

citations.quote: the idea behind it was to utilize really the fundamental basis of crypto which is disintermediation between advertisers publishers and users
the notifications achieved a CTR of 3.24% which is very strong
Learn about the Polkadot DAO: https://polkadot.com/platform/dao

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: crypto assets, wallets and private keys, a token sale, multi-chain settlement, global advertising, and direct ecosystem links. The speakers emphasize that Brave raised “around $30 million in around 30 seconds” through a token sale, discuss managing wallets and private keys, and describe BAT and Solana settlement. Those details give the promotion the appearance of technical legitimacy while directing viewers toward Polkadot resources and participation. The campaign also reports very large exposure and strong click activity, increasing the scale at which viewers could be steered into crypto involvement.

citations.quote: we raised around $30 million in around 30 seconds
it really taught me the fundamentals of crypto in the sense of managing wallets and private keys
we also evolved to have Solana as well
that led to 141 million views
Explore all things technical: https://wiki.polkadot.network/

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presentation’s technical vocabulary and impressive reach can make the promotion look authoritative, but neither proves that the promoted assets are safe. The speakers themselves say Brave loses visibility after a user leaves the browser, and they could not report downloads from their side. Thus the reported views and clicks show distribution, not a verified beneficial outcome for participants.

citations.quote: once a user exits our app you know browser is essentially an app once they exit that we lose that visibility
we wouldn't be able to, on our end, report what's going on once a person leaves the browser experience
that led to 141 million views

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Crypto terminology alone is not a promise of appreciation, dividends, or profit. The token-sale history is presented as background to Brave’s advertising model, and the campaign data is openly qualified: Brave cannot guarantee that survey respondents saw an ad and cannot track activity after users leave. The evidence therefore shows a disclosed advertising campaign, not deceptive asset-return solicitation.

if that Dapp has tracking on their end, they have that first-party analytics

opening.argument: Although presented as a discussion and report, the video functions as a polished promotional presentation. The speakers identify a campaign objective to drive participation, show notification ads and landing-page examples, report extensive views and clicks, and provide resources for getting started with Polkadot. They also emphasize that Brave managed the campaign and used Polkadot’s imagery and guidelines. This combination turns apparent education into endorsement: the audience is not simply learning about crypto, but being guided toward a branded ecosystem and its projects through an advertising funnel.

citations.quote: we completely managed the entire campaign from our end, but we utilised the imagery and the guidelines and the colours of the ecosystem
the proposal included about 12 new tip takeovers
three to four brave users are at least somewhat likely to participate in Polkadot projects
Explore the Polkadot platform: https://polkadot.com/platform

rebuttal.rebuttal: The educational format is precisely what makes the promotion persuasive. The opening describes the event as a campaign discussion, but the presentation shows ad formats, creative, targeting, and performance, while the linked resources invite further Polkadot engagement. Calling the material a report does not change that its stated aim was to increase participation in projects.

citations.quote: Today we are happy to have with us the team from Brave Browser. And they're here to discuss a recent campaign that they ran for the Polkadot ecosystem on Brave.
newsfeed ads educate the audience and the notification ads aim to convert the users
the text in them is the ad itself

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion of an advertising service is not the same as fraudulent promotion of token returns. The speakers explain the campaign’s formats and limitations, including that downloads require cooperation with the individual project and that Brave cannot track activity outside its browser. The resources identify Polkadot channels and documentation, but no cited material promises appreciation, dividends, or guaranteed income.
